verdict.line: You lose if you overextend before level 6 into his Q-stack-into-W stun combo; you win if you land full Hemorrhage stacks and drag the lane into extended trades.

brief.thesis: Darius wins this lane by completing the 5-stack Hemorrhage combo and riding E (Apprehend)'s armor-shred passive through a champion who wants to stack tank items; K'Sante wins it by using Q (Ntofo Strikes) stacks into W (Path Maker)'s stun to cut a trade short before stacks finish and punish any overextension with a solo kill. The 53.5% head-to-head over 2478 games says you're slightly favored, but the measured solo-kill edge sits with K'Sante — this is a lane about surviving his burst windows, not avoiding him entirely.

theirWindow.when: K'Sante at 2 Q stacks with W up
theirWindow.what: At 2 stacks his Q fires a shockwave that pulls you in, which he can chain directly into Path Maker's stun. Back off or bait the second stack onto a minion before you let him poke you.

yourWindow.what: Footwork is his only shield and gap-close/disengage tool, on an 8-10s cooldown. Commit your E (Apprehend, 535 range) to pull him in during that window — he has nothing to escape the follow-up combo with.

start.why: 53.1% win rate over 2487 games at an 85.7% pick rate — the extra sustain and early damage keep you even through K'Sante's Q poke while your Hemorrhage procs tick for more.

boots.why: 52% win rate over 1796 games at a 64.8% pick rate — flat damage reduction cuts into both his repeated Q pokes and his auto-attacks once he's stacked Ntofo Strikes.

core.why: The active haste closes the gap on Footwork dashes and lets you force the stack combo on your terms.
Move speed stacking keeps you attached through his disengage attempts so stacks don't fall off mid-combo.

situational.when: you fall behind in lane and need the extra health and tenacity to survive his All Out burst window
the game runs long and you want stacking armor shred on top of E's passive to keep deleting his resistances

runes.keystoneWhy: Stacking adaptive force through repeated Q/E/auto contact rewards exactly the extended-trade playstyle this lane calls for, and the healing offsets his Footwork shield sustain. Master-tier players run Stormraider's Surge instead across 17,974 games — that suits a more mobile, pick-and-run Darius who leans on E's pull range rather than grinding out full 5-stack combos.

summoners.why: Flash+Ghost (53.4% win rate, 79.1% pick rate) gives you the sustained speed to stay attached through Footwork dashes and land E's pull before he resets distance. Flash+Ignite (52.6%, 17.5% pick) is the better call if you're confident forcing all-ins and want the true damage to finish kills through his shield.

playing.title: Outrange his poke with E
playing.detail: Your E (Apprehend) reaches 535 range against his Q's 450 — hover just outside his Q and punish any overextension with a pull before he can poke you first.

playing.title: Track Footwork's cooldown
playing.detail: Only commit your E pull inside Footwork's 8-10s cooldown window; outside it he can shield and disengage out of your combo for free.

playing.title: Respect the 2-stack shockwave
playing.detail: Don't stand in Q range once he's at 1 stack — the 2nd stack fires a pull shockwave that chains straight into Path Maker's stun.

playing.title: Punish the W channel
playing.detail: Path Maker requires a windup before the dash-stun. Use that channel to land Q's blade and start W (Crippling Strike)'s slow so he can't close cleanly.

playing.title: Hold R for the true damage reset
playing.detail: Noxian Guillotine's cooldown refreshes briefly on a kill and ignores his shields — save it to finish through Footwork rather than opening with it.

playing.title: Stack to 5 before you back off
playing.detail: Hemorrhage's enrage at 5 stacks is where trades flip hardest in your favor, since the bleed ticks through his shield regardless.

playing.title: Track his ultimate timer
playing.detail: All Out's 120/100/80/80/80s cooldown knocks you through walls before he goes all-in — don't get caught alone in lane once it's up.

brief.patchCaveat: The build order, runes, boots, and summoner spells above are pulled directly from measured games on the current patch; the lane mechanics, timing windows, and tell-reading are my own tactical analysis layered on top of that data.
